drafts.title: Cup holders fit common bottles and hold them secure while driving
drafts.description: Customers can place common bottle and tumbler sizes in the cup holders without forcing or tipping, and bottles remain upright and stable during normal driving.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Cup holders must accept bottles up to 90 mm diameter and 750 ml volume and retain them without tipping during a 0.5 g lateral acceleration test in at least 95% of trials.
assumptions: 90 mm diameter and 750 ml represent common bottle/tumbler sizes in target markets.
Verification uses standard ISO vehicle dynamics test rig for 0.5 g lateral acceleration.
uncertainties: Emerging bottle form factors (very tall/slim designs) may exceed 90 mm and require different holder geometries.

drafts.title: Hands-free tailgate opens reliably on the first attempt in normal conditions
drafts.description: When a customer uses the hands-free tailgate gesture at normal approach speeds and distances, the tailgate opens reliably without repeated attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Tailgate opens on the first valid gesture in at least 95% of attempts across 100 standardized trials covering gait speeds 0.5–1.5 m/s and approach distances 30–120 cm in dry and light-rain conditions.
assumptions: Standardized gesture detection area and timing will be defined for validation tests.
Tests exclude blocked or intentional failure modes (e.g., locked vehicle).
uncertainties: Performance in heavy rain, deep snow or with obstructive clothing may degrade; separate validation required for those conditions.

drafts.title: Ambient lighting offers many colors, fine brightness control and user presets
drafts.description: Customers can select from a broad palette and adjust brightness in fine steps, and save personal presets so interior ambient lighting matches their preference anytime.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: System provides at least 64 distinct color options, at least 10 discrete brightness levels from low to high, and allows saving at least three user presets; verified through UI tests.
assumptions: Customers value color variety and brightness granularity for personalization.
Color choices are presented in a user-friendly UI with fine-grained controls.
uncertainties: Perceived color differences depend on material reflectance and may vary across lighting locations.

drafts.title: Front seats provide longer adjustable thigh support for tall drivers
drafts.description: Tall drivers can extend the front seat cushion to achieve comfortable thigh support so longer legs are supported without pressure points at the cushion edge.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Front seats include an adjustable thigh-support extension of at least 50 mm of usable support range, validated with anthropometric manikins representing drivers up to 195 cm tall achieving even pressure distribution across the cushion.
assumptions: 50 mm extension is effective to address complaints from taller drivers without compromising other seat ergonomics.
Anthropometric manikins and pressure-mapping equipment are available for validation.
uncertainties: Extreme body shapes may still require bespoke seating; packaging constraints with heated/cooled seats may limit extension designs.

drafts.title: Seat memory restores saved seating positions reliably and repeatably
drafts.description: When a customer recalls a saved seat position, the seat returns to the stored position quickly and within tight positional tolerances across repeated uses.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Seat memory recall restores the saved position within ±10 mm linear and ±1° angular tolerance within 5 seconds on at least 95% of 100 consecutive recall attempts during warm and cold cabin conditions.
assumptions: Tolerance levels ±10 mm/±1° reflect customer expectations for 'same position'.
Validation includes multiple environmental temperature conditions to capture thermal effects on actuators.
uncertainties: Long-term wear or electrical noise could reduce repeatability and may need durability testing to quantify drift over vehicle lifetime.

drafts.title: Flush door handles operate reliably in freezing winter conditions
drafts.description: Customers can open the vehicle with the external door handle in freezing weather without manual de-icing or repeated attempts.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Flush door handles must operate and open in at least 95% of attempts after exposure to −20 °C ambient and an ice accretion scenario with up to 3 mm surface ice, verified over 50 cycles.
assumptions: −20 °C and 3 mm ice accretion represent common severe-freezing conditions for target markets.
Validation tests will simulate realistic freezing/defrost cycles.
uncertainties: Extreme salt/road-debris accumulation or physical damage could still impair operation; user maintenance instructions may help mitigate.

drafts.title: Rear seating legroom is at least as generous as main competitors in the segment
drafts.description: Rear-seat passengers experience legroom that matches or exceeds primary rivals so passengers do not feel cramped compared with alternatives in the segment.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Measured rear knee clearance (knee point to front seat back) is within ±10 mm of the average of the top three segment competitors, and must not be smaller than that average in benchmark testing.
assumptions: Benchmark competitor models and measurement methods will be selected according to industry-standard procedures.
Packaging trade-offs (battery, drivetrain) are managed to preserve rear occupant space.
uncertainties: Future competitor packaging changes may shift the benchmark upward; continuous market monitoring will be needed before launch.

drafts.title: Trunk includes an accessible power outlet to run common portable coolers
drafts.description: Customers can plug a portable cooler into a socket in the trunk and run it while the vehicle is parked without needing extra adapters or routing power from the cabin.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Provide a trunk-located 12 V outlet capable of supplying at least 40 W continuous for typical portable coolers, with protected cabling and an IP-cover; operation verified under parked conditions.
assumptions: Typical portable cooler draws ~30–40 W; providing 40 W covers the common device set.
Socket placement and cover ensure safe use and prevent water ingress while loading cargo.
uncertainties: High-draw accessories or multiple simultaneous draws may require higher capacity or fused protection beyond this baseline.

drafts.title: Pedestrian protection compliance request (regulatory scope)
drafts.description: Customers asked that the front end meets the new EU pedestrian protection regulation; this item documents the request but regulatory compliance is out of product-definition scope here.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Documented customer request; regulatory compliance decisions and certification activities are handled under homologation and legal scopes, not in this customer-facing requirement set.
assumptions: Regulatory compliance is necessary but belongs to homologation/engineering workstreams.
uncertainties: Specific technical responses required to meet the regulation may impact styling and packaging.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/homologation request — out of scope for customer-facing product requirements; addressed in homologation engineering.

drafts.title: Rear-seat airbag FMVSS 208 certification request (regulatory scope)
drafts.description: Customers want rear seat airbags to obtain FMVSS 208 certification; this request is documented but certification activities are handled in homologation.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Documented customer request; certification activities and test methods are managed in homologation and engineering scopes.
assumptions: FMVSS 208 is a regulatory standard requiring engineering and test validation outside the product outcome definitions here.
uncertainties: Design changes to meet FMVSS 208 could impact interior packaging and cost.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/certification request — out of scope for customer-facing requirement definitions.

drafts.title: Headlight beam pattern compliance request (regulatory scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that headlights follow ECE R112 beam pattern rules in every market; this is a regulatory request documented here for homologation workstreams.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Documented customer request; market-specific beam pattern approvals and certification activities are handled by homologation teams.
assumptions: ECE R112 compliance requires engineering certification per market and is executed by homologation.
uncertainties: Global harmonization of beam patterns may not be possible due to differing market regulations.
drafts.scope_reason: Regulation/homologation request — outside product requirement drafting scope.

drafts.title: Magnetic rotary encoder 12-bit request (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers requested the volume knob use a 12-bit magnetic rotary encoder; this is a component-level engineering specification and is recorded out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Documented customer request for 12-bit magnetic encoder; selection and implementation are engineering decisions.
assumptions: Implementation and supplier selection are engineering tasks tied to HMI feel and noise budgets.
uncertainties: Alternate approaches (software filtering, haptics) could meet the underlying customer need for precise volume control.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific component request — engineering specification out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Side window laminated glass thickness request (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers requested 4.5 mm thick laminated side glass; this is a specific material/part specification and is recorded out of scope for customer-facing requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Documented customer request for 4.5 mm laminated glass; material specification and trade-offs (weight, NVH) are engineering decisions.
assumptions: Glass thickness affects NVH and safety; feasibility and weight impact to be evaluated by engineering.
uncertainties: Achieving 4.5 mm laminated glass globally may affect production cost and weight targets.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific material/component request — engineering specification out of scope.

drafts.title: Seat foam density 55 kg/m³ request (engineering spec)
drafts.description: Customers asked that seat cushions use foam with a density of 55 kg/m³; this specific material requirement is recorded but treated as an engineering specification.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Documented customer request for 55 kg/m³ foam density; final material selection, durability and NVH trade-offs to be decided by engineering.
assumptions: Specified foam density affects comfort, durability and cost and requires validation in seat development.
Customer preference implies desire for firmer support.
uncertainties: Perceived comfort depends on foam construction, layering and seat geometry, not density alone.
drafts.scope_reason: Specific component/material request — engineering specification out of scope for customer-facing requirements.

drafts.title: Residual value guarantee request (business/financial scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that BMW guarantees a residual value of 60% after five years; this is a financial/business request and outside product technical requirements.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Documented customer request for a 60% five-year residual value guarantee; pricing, finance and warranty policies to be evaluated by commercial teams.
assumptions: Residual value guarantees implicate finance, residual risk and warranty/legal teams.
uncertainties: Market volatility and option/content mix can influence achievable residual values.
drafts.scope_reason: Business/financial request — out of scope for product feature requirements.

drafts.title: Request to cut production cost per car by 8% (business/engineering scope)
drafts.description: Customers ask that BMW reduce production cost per car by 8%; this is a commercial/production target rather than a customer-facing capability and is recorded out of scope here.
drafts.acceptance_criterion: Documented customer request to reduce production cost by 8%; cost-reduction programs and their impact on product features are managed by manufacturing and finance.
assumptions: Production cost targets are set by internal cost and program teams and may trade off features or materials.
uncertainties: Achieving cost reductions without impacting perceived quality requires targeted program work outside product requirement scope.
drafts.scope_reason: Business/production cost target — out of scope for customer-facing requirement drafting.
